Triage notes so far (initial):
- Ingress telemetry indicates a concurrent rise in SYN retransmits and DNS query latency spikes for the region serving MerchantLane.
- No config rollouts on our control plane between 07:30-08:30 UTC; infra change windows show nothing in that window.
- Early hypothesis: AS-path flap or VPC peering NAT pool exhaustion causing heavy retransmits + longer RTTs; also seeing elevated upstream DNS timeouts to the resolver set used by that customer’s region.

Requests for MerchantLane SRE:
- Please run: traceroute --tcp -p 443 api.redwood.ai from an affected host and paste output.
- Capture a short named pcap filtered to src/dst and include the three-way handshake time.

Ben — can you pull NAT session counters and resolver error rate for the peering edge for tenant ML-42? I’ll compare to historical baselines.

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Latency spike + 5xx surge impacting payment flows

Update from edge metrics and DNS team:
- We’re seeing elevated DNS NXDOMAIN/REFUSED ratios from resolvers servicing the merchantlane vpc peering (match in time with 07:50 UTC).
- NAT session tallies at the peering gateway jumped ~6x and hit soft limits; a small subset of connections were dropped/retried causing higher request latencies and 5xx responses when backends saw incomplete TLS handshakes.
- Correlated the retransmits in their pcap with our egress logs — many flows had RTT spikes coincident with the ASN-flap reported by Priya.

Short-term mitigations applied (15:55 UTC):
- Opened a temporary direct route for MerchantLane traffic to an alternate egress node (bypasses suspect ASN path).
- Increased NAT session soft-limit for that peering for the next 3 hours.

Result: error rate dropped from ~40% to ~6% within ~8 minutes of mitigation; tail latency improved but not fully back to baseline. Continuing monitoring.

Action items:
- Postmortem to include: peering asymmetry, resolver hardening, and NAT headroom policy.
- Recommend scheduled window with MerchantLane networking team to provision a redundant egress path.

Ben Carter
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Jonas — brief summary and exec request:

Summary:
- Impact window: ~07:50–08:10 UTC; main customer impact seen in throughput collapse and ~40% 5xx for payment flows.
- Root contributors (preliminary): asymmetric peering path through ASN 32999 causing retransmits, combined with MerchantLane egress NAT pool change which reduced available sessions and amplified retries. Secondary contributor: elevated DNS timeouts from resolver set.
- Mitigation: temporary alternate egress route + increased NAT soft-limits; reduced error rate to ~6% and improved tail latency.

Customer ask: MerchantLane is requesting a formal credit and an on-site (virtual) postmortem with networking folks. They are a strategic commerce customer on a committed plan (deal ML-2024-ENTERPRISE-42).

Recommendation / ask:
- Approve a one-time service credit of 30% for the impacted billing period as a goodwill gesture and to preserve relationship. (Marissa, please advise on final amount and T&C.)
- Ownership: Vivek to lead technical postmortem; Marissa to lead customer comms and credit execution.
- Logistics: propose a 60-min postmortem meeting on Thu 17 Jun 2027 with MerchantLane SRE + our network eng. I’ll coordinate and send invites.

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for rapid pairing. We’ll publish a detailed postmortem in the Drive link and schedule the review.
